comment.WORKFLOWS: Select workflows you want to run, possible values: FETCH, MAPPING, QC, DEDUP, TRIMMING, COUNTING, TRACKS, PEAKS, DE, DEU, DAS, DTU, CIRCS, FUSIONS
comment.BINS: Where to find the scripts used in the workflow, per default the scripts directory that comes with MONSDA. ONLY CHANGE IF YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE DOING!
comment.MAXTHREADS: Maximum number of cores to use, make sure this fits your needs, acts as upper cap.
comment.VERSION: Version of MONSDA to use, needs to match installed version
comment.POSTDE: Optional post-DE enrichment/regulatory analysis (GO/GSEA/GSVA/decoupleR/dream). Disabled by default. When enabled, 'config' must point to a PostDE analysis JSON (see configs/postde_analysis.json). Only supported with the DE workflow and the deseq2/edger DE tools.

comment.GROUPS: Please enter a comma separated list of the groups your samples belong to. This does not have to be in any relation with the condition-tree but is used solely to establish contrasts for differential analysis. Each sample needs a matching entry. Can be left blank to run all-vs-all comparison.
comment.TYPES: Please enter a comma separated list for this setting matching your sample list, i.e. each sample should have a matching entry. Can be left blank.
comment.BATCHES: Please enter a comma separated list for this setting matching your sample list, i.e. each sample should have a matching entry. Can be left blank.
comment.SEQUENCING: single or paired or singlecell and stranded info [rf,fr,ff,unstranded (or empty)] comma separated
comment.REFERENCE: set path to reference, '.fa', '.fa.gz' or '.fa.bgz' ending expected
comment.DECOY: set path to decoy file if tool for mapping/counting needs decoys, like e.g. salmon
comment.INDEX: set path to index, default index to use for mapping with this settings
comment.PREFIX: if needed, prefix for mapping software can be set here
comment.GTF: set path to gtf, '.gtf', '.gtf.gz' or '.gtf.bgz' ending expected, THIS WILL BE USED WHENEVER POSSIBLE OR NOT DEFINED OTHERWISE
comment.GFF: set path to gff, '.gff', '.gff.gz' or '.gff.bgz' ending expected. THIS WILL BE USED WHEN GTF IS NOT AVAILABLE BUT ANNOTATION IS REQUIRED OR IF TOOL REQUIRES GFF FORMAT
comment.IP: OPTIONAL if PEAKS is run and files need specific processing, eg. for iCLIP protocol

comment.COUNTTOOL: Gene-level counting tool used for DE, like the TOOLS key but for the counting step. 'featureCounts' for short-read BAMs (default). 'oarfish' aggregates long-read (PacBio/Nanopore) transcript-level quantification from the genome-mapped BAM to gene level.
comment.COUNT: Options for read counting, independent of COUNTS workflows, utilizes FeatureCounts
comment.QUANT: oarfish quant options, only used when COUNTTOOL is 'oarfish'
comment.DE: Options for DE Analysis as key=value pairs. 'controlgenes=<file>' is a file with one spike-in/control gene ID per line. Setting it does not change the standard analysis, it adds two more readings of every contrast: '_norm' uses the control genes as size factors (absolute, per cell fold changes) and '_ruv' adds the RUVg factors of unwanted variation W_1..W_k to the design while keeping the standard normalization (RUVSeq vignette). Control genes are never tested themselves. 'ruvk=auto|<integer>' sets the number of RUVg factors, default 'auto' estimates it from the control genes by a permutation test on the variance spectrum, 'ruvk=0' drops the W covariates so that '_ruv' reproduces the standard branch. The per-k diagnostics are written to *_table_ruv_k_selection.tsv and *_figure_RUV_k_selection.png. 'design=<formula>' sets the model formula per contrast, e.g. 'design=batch+condition' (the leading ~ is optional). It may use condition, type and batch, which are filled from GROUPS, TYPES and BATCHES, must contain condition and must keep the intercept. Without it MONSDA derives the design from the types and batches present in the two groups. Terms that are not estimable for a given contrast are dropped with a warning
